race: Formula 1 Singapore Airlines Singapore Grand Prix 2026

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Welcome to The Race Weekend Podcast, because Singapore is about to turn into a night of heat, chaos, and championship noise, and we are ready for it.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: First, the heat hazard has been declared for the fourth time this season, and it is the second weekend in a row, so expect extra care with tyres and engines.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: So the drivers are managing engines and tyres before the lights even come on, and that changes every lap, every stint, and every chance to attack.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Then we had that glitch that turned Formula One into a Lego race, and Hamilton and Verstappen were bemused by it, which is exactly the kind of moment we love.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: I love that those two can share a funny moment, but Sunday will be a completely different story, and the points race will not care about the jokes.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: And the engine chat is still buzzing, with V eight turbo engines appearing on the horizon for the future of Formula One, which gives the whole weekend a strange extra edge.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Three quick news bits, but the real question is who wins under the lights when the championship gets loud and the street circuit starts to bite.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Let's start with Kimi Antonelli, because the data says first with the championship leader, eight wins, and strong street form, so we cannot ignore that.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: But his history here is thin, one race, one fifth, and no podium yet, so this is a test of nerve on a track that punishes hesitation.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: So this is a medium confidence pick, not a lock, and that is why we are debating it rather than just nodding along like it is obvious.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: I am not buying it until he proves he can turn street form into a Singapore result that matters, and I want to see that in qualifying.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Then Max Verstappen, two podiums from three starts here, best second, and he has been dominant in Malaysia, so the record book is on his side.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: That Singapore record is the reason he is in the top three, not just because he is Max, and that is a fair point, but it is not the whole story.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Right, and his confidence is doing a lot of the work, especially on a street circuit where one mistake can cost you the whole afternoon.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: My top three pick is Lando Norris, with three podiums in three starts here, including a win, and that is the kind of history that makes you nervous.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: That is the cleanest circuit history in our top ten, average second and best first, so the data is smiling, and we should not ignore it.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: So how do you beat that? I mean, if the data is this clean, what is your counter argument?

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: You do not, unless Mercedes finds a street circuit trick that nobody else has, the rain stays out, and Kimi happens to have the perfect car.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Deep cut time, because Isack Hadjar in seventh is the low confidence gamble, and I kind of like that, because it is the kind of pick that can explode.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Red Bull pace and recent top five finishes make him the one to watch, even if we are not fully sure, and that uncertainty is part of the fun.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: I would not bet the house on it, but a low confidence pick is where the fun starts, and it makes the top ten feel more alive.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: The other low confidence story is a Racing Bulls double in eighth and ninth, with Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad, and that is a bit of a surprise.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Now Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc are both in the top five because Ferrari has been strong and consistent, and that keeps the front packed.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: That keeps the top ten tight, and it makes the deep cut feel even more dangerous, because one good lap can change the whole picture.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: We have the top three, the deep cut, and now the full list, so let's make it quick and loud before the lights come on.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Give us the run, Paul, and remind us why this top ten is both exciting and a little bit risky.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Here is the full top ten, Kimi Antonelli, Max Verstappen, Lando Norris, Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc, Oscar Piastri, Isack Hadjar, Liam Lawson, Arvid Lindblad, and Pierre Gasly, so put your lights on, because Singapore is about to get loud and fast.
